reply.title: Squashing with the Logistic Curve
reply.story: When modeling probabilities or neural networks, we often need to turn any input from negative infinity to positive infinity into a clean probability between zero and one. Early biometricians studying population growth noticed that growth starts exponential but caps out due to limited resources, forming an S-shaped curve. By dividing one by the sum of one and the exponential of negative input, we get a smooth function that compresses vast ranges into a tight interval. Adjusting the steepness parameter changes how sharply the transition happens around the midpoint, letting us control the sensitivity of the response.
reply.cardDescription: Discover how the logistic sigmoid maps any real input into a bounded range between $0$ and $1$. See how adjusting the steepness parameter shapes the transition.
reply.instructions: Adjust the steepness slider to change how fast the curve transitions from zero to one. Observe the output value at the fixed marker.
